observations: Nikon DSLR camera body with a neck strap.
One lens is mounted on the camera; a second lens is placed beside it.
The mounted lens features a manual aperture ring, characteristic of older Nikon AF-D series lenses.
The camera body has the signature Nikon red 'swoosh' on the handgrip.
The model name badge on the front of the camera is obscured by shadow.
No battery, charger, or memory cards are visible.

claims.evidence: Two lenses are present, but the text on the lens barrels identifying focal lengths is not legible.
The photo is taken from a distance; internal dust, fungus in lenses, or sensor marks cannot be seen.
Video capability depends entirely on the model; many older Nikon DSLRs (e.g., D40, D60, D70, D80) do not record video.

risks.risk: Unknown model determines the base value
risks.proof: A clear photo of the front of the camera showing the model number (e.g., D3100, D5200, D90).
Close-up photos of the front and rear glass elements of both lenses.
A screenshot of the shutter count from a tool like 'myshuttercount' using the last photo taken.
A photo of a clear blue sky or white wall taken at a high aperture (f/22).
Photo of the battery and the wall charger.

proof_requests: Photo of the front of the camera showing the model name (e.g., D3200).
Photos of the glass on both lenses to check for fungus.
Photo of the battery and charger.
The current shutter count of the camera.
response.reason: The model of the camera is not visible in the photo. Because Nikon DSLR values range from very low for older models to significant for newer ones, and because some older models cannot record video as claimed, the model must be identified before a price can be set.
